newsitem.title: USA: Woman Air Force pilot missing in Arizona crash.
newsitem.headline: Woman Air Force pilot missing in Arizona crash.

text.p: The woman pilot of a U.S. Air Force A-10 attack jet was missing on Wednesday after her aircraft crashed at a training range in southwest Arizona on Tuesday night, the Air Force said.

The missing pilot of the single-seat fighter was identified as Air Force Capt. Amy Lynn Svoboda. She was on a routine training mission from Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Arizona when the crash occurred.

The crash occurred at the Barry Goldwater Training Range at about 9:30 p.m. local time. The Air Force said the A-10, designed to destroy tanks and other armor, was carrying six 25-pound practice bombs that emit smoke and a small flash on contact with the ground for accuracy evaluation.
Air Force officials and safety experts were traveling to the crash site to ensure the safety of the scene before a recovery team could begin to sort through the wreckage.
Svoboda is assigned to the 355th fighter squadron and has been at Davis-Monthan for about a year, Air Force officials said.
